description: Scale-free k(A) form test: inverting exact w_std(k) against AME B(A) ratios (ref=2H), k_implied is strongly sub-linear in A -> falsifies naive k~A and k~bond-count; best-fitting named form is logarithmic. Constrains GAP-A-3 to a log-type rule; no scale, no wiring, no closure.

assertions.name: k_implied_strongly_sublinear_in_A
assertions.detail: A spans x8.0 (2->16) while k_implied spans only x2.84 (3.00->8.52) -> STRONGLY sub-linear; naive k~A and k~bond-count FALSIFIED (a-scope)

assertions.name: log_forms_beat_linear
assertions.detail: k~log A R^2=0.863 beats k~A R^2=0.672 and k~bonds R^2=0.485 (best-fitting NAMED form: 'k ~ log(bond count)')

result.verdict: k(A) FORM CONSTRAINED (scale-free, no closure): inverting the exact tower weight w_std(k) against AME B(A) ratios (ref=2H), the implied level k_implied(A) is STRONGLY SUB-LINEAR in A (A x8, k only x2.8) — so the naive k~A and k~bond-count candidates are FALSIFIED (a-scope). The best-fitting named form is 'k ~ log(bond count)' (R^2=0.891); k~log A (R^2=0.863) clearly beats linear. NOTE log A and log(bond-count) are statistically INDISTINGUISHABLE here (both ~0.87-0.89, near-collinear for these nuclei) — the robust claim is LOG-TYPE, not log-A-vs-log-bonds. This is the arithmetic consequence of w_std growing super-geometrically while B is ~extensive: the jet level grows ~log(mass). GAP-A-3 is thereby constrained to a LOG-TYPE k(A). Sets no scale, wires nothing, lands no magnitude; the open piece is WHY k(A)~log from the drivers. Light nuclei are below saturation so residual scatter (R^2~0.88, not ~1) is expected.

context.open_object: GAP-A-3 level selection k(A); constrains its FORM to log-type
